Share SOC2 Type II report and network/VPC diagram
Schedule a 2-hour benchmark run with our sample prompts on Dedicated trial instances
Follow up with proposed SLA and onboarding timeline by Friday 2025-07-18
action_items: Jordan Park: send detailed pricing and reserved instance amortization sheet (due 2025-07-18)
Camila Ruiz: compile benchmark checklist and test dataset, coordinate trial run (due 2025-07-21)

summary: Discovery focused on Dedicated capacity: Novatech needs reserved GPUs with burst capability, VPC isolation, and predictable autoscaling. Key concerns: latency SLOs, cost modeling vs hosted, enterprise security (KMS, audit logs), and integration timeline. Agreed to run benchmarks on Dedicated trial and share SOC2/network diagrams.
questions: What are realistic throughput targets per GPU for our model mix?
How does burst capacity billing work?
Can we get isolated tenancy (no multi-tenant on same host)?
What's the expected lead time for Dedicated provisioning?
transcript:
Header: Novatech Dedicated Capacity Discovery
Date: 2025-07-14
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Camila Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (Novatech Head of ML), Maya Lin (Novatech Platform Eng), Evan Brooks (Novatech CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. I'm Jordan Park from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Camila Ruiz, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:10] Sanjay: Good, thanks. Excited to dive in. We sent over some notes about our expected throughput, hopefully we can go into sizing.
[00:18] Camila: Yep, saw the doc, thanks. Quick agenda: we want to understand your model mix, latency goals, security constraints, and then talk about Dedicated sizing and burst strategy. Sound OK?
[00:27] Maya: Sounds good. I'll just flag network is a big piece for us — we need VPC peering or private link and strict egress controls.
[00:35] Evan: Also want to understand if we can get physical isolation or at least single-tenant hosts for compliance reasons.
[00:42] Jordan: Great, that's helpful context. Sanjay, can you walk us through the models and traffic pattern?
[00:47] Sanjay: Sure. We're running two families: a 7B generation model for chat-like customer interactions and a 13B for higher-fidelity summarization. Peak is around 1200 concurrent requests during spikes; average is 250. Token distribution skews to 80 tokens per request for generation, 512 for long-form summarization but that's rarer.
[01:10] Camila: OK so mixed sequence lengths. For Dedicated, we typically size by concurrent prompts and token/sec — and we apply continuous batching. Quick question, are you currently quantizing models?
[01:20] Sanjay: We're evaluating 4-bit but haven't fully committed. Cost is a concern; if quant helps us hit throughput, we will.
[01:27] Jordan: On pricing, we'll break down amortized reserved GPU cost vs hosted per-token. Usually Dedicated is best when steady baseline usage exists and you want control. Burst covers the top percentiles.
[01:36] Maya: About burst — we need to understand billing and how bursting affects latency. In our tests with other providers, burst meant degraded latency.
[01:45] Camila: Right, so our burst model is configurable: you reserve X GPUs for baseline and then have burst capacity that can spin up on the same cluster or in a pre-warmed pool. Billing is a combination — reserved seat amortized monthly plus burst usage billed at a premium per GPU-hour. We also have a burst credit model for predictable monthly bursts.
[02:06] Evan: Is the burst pool multi-tenant? For us, isolation is a requirement for certain data flows.
[02:12] Camila: Good callout. We can offer isolated burst pools in Dedicated — it's an optional configuration. If you need strict tenancy, we can provision single-tenant hosts. It increases cost but meets compliance.
[02:24] Sanjay: How about autoscaling speed? We care about latency so slow scale-ups kill our SLA.
[02:30] Camila: We support fast scale though there's tradeoffs: warm pools reduce cold-start but cost more. We do continuous batching and KV cache reuse which shortens response times for cache hits. For cold path, spin-up is usually in the 30–90 second range depending on hardware. We can do warm standby for critical routes.
[02:50] Jordan: Also our smart routing can send traffic to hosted fallback or lower-cost variants if Dedicated is saturated — useful in outages.
[02:58] Maya: Could you explain the hosted fallback? That's interesting but may run into data residency issues.
[03:04] Camila: It's policy-driven. For example, non-sensitive requests can go to hosted, sensitive ones stay in Dedicated. We can mark routes. If data residency prevents it, we can instead route to another Dedicated pool in a compliant region.
[03:18] Sanjay: On the security front: KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO are must-haves. We're SOC2 and ISO oriented.
[03:25] Jordan: We have KMS/HSM integrations, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs with export. We'll attach the SOC2 Type II and architecture diagrams.
[03:33] Evan: Lead time — how long from signed order to Dedicated being live?
[03:37] Camila: Typical provisioning for Dedicated is 2–4 weeks for common configs if we're using cloud-backed capacity. For on-prem or air-gapped, obviously longer. If you want single-tenant physical hosts, tack on an extra week for procurement and placement.
[03:52] Sanjay: Hm, okay. Could we start with a smaller Dedicated baseline and rely on burst while we ramp?
[03:58] Jordan: That's a common approach: commit to X GPUs baseline and have burst credits. We'll model the economics two ways.
[04:05] Maya: For throughput numbers, what's realistic per A100 equivalent for your 13B and 7B families?
[04:12] Camila: Ballpark: optimized 7B at FP16/quant can do several hundred tokens/sec depending on batching; 13B lower. We'll run a benchmark with your prompt set to get precise numbers. There will be some variance with sequence lengths.
[04:28] Sanjay: Good. We need to bring this to the infra team — they care about egress, subnets, and peering.
[04:34] Jordan: We'll include a network diagram and step-by-step for VPC peering and private link.
[04:39] [05:00] Speaker 1 (transcription noise): mm-hmm
[05:05] Camila: Quick note on KV caching — for chat-like loads where prefixes repeat, caching can reduce token compute significantly. We recommend a prefix cache for interactive chat.
[05:18] Sanjay: That might help our cost. For summarization jobs we batch offline on Dedicated.
[05:25] Camila: Also recommend quant profiles per model; we can provide suggested quant and kernel combos in the Optimize reports.
[05:33] Evan: For SLA, what's your 99th percentile latency guarantee?
[05:37] Jordan: For Dedicated we can contract custom SLOs; typical targets are p95 < 350ms for short requests on pre-warmed instances but depends on model complexity. We'll want to baseline in the trial.
[05:50] Maya: Is there tracing and per-request observability we can integrate with our APM?
[05:55] Camila: Yes — request-level tracing, per-route dashboards, latency and token cost breakdowns, and we can forward traces to your tracing system.
[06:06] Sanjay: About data retention: we can't have logs stored in hosted buckets for certain customers. Can logs be kept in-customer-controlled storage?
[06:14] Camila: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to your S3/GCS or to a customer-managed logging endpoint.
[06:21] Jordan: Let's talk numbers briefly — Sanjay you mentioned average 250 concurrent. To size baseline, are you comfortable committing to a baseline that covers say 60% of peak?
[06:30] Sanjay: Possibly. We need modeling to show cost impact. If baseline too high it's wasted, too low and burst costs blow up.
[06:38] Camila: We'll provide a sensitivity analysis. Also you can set burst caps to limit surprise spend.
[06:45] [07:05] Maya: One operational question: how are model rollouts handled? We need canary and automatic fallback.
[07:12] Camila: Rollouts supported — canary percent traffic, A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions or latency breaches. You can pin a route to a model version.
[07:21] Evan: For compliance we will need audit trails of who triggered rollouts.
[07:24] Jordan: That's in the audit logs. We can also add role-based approvals for production releases.
[07:31] Sanjay: Any hidden constraints — like we have custom kernels or specific ops?
[07:36] Camila: We handle standard transformer ops. If you have custom ops we'll need to validate; sometimes that requires a runtime build. We can take an evaluation bundle.
[07:46] [08:10] Speaker 2 (crosstalk): yeah, uh-huh
[08:14] Camila: For the benchmark, we'll need your sample prompt set, sequence length distribution, and a representative request trace. Then we'll run on Dedicated trial GPUs and share perf and cost per token.
[08:27] Sanjay: We'll provide that. Timeline: can the trial be scheduled next week?
[08:31] Camila: We can queue a trial — provisioning for trial instances is faster, often 48–72 hours.
[08:38] Maya: Who will own the trial on Redwood side?
[08:41] Camila: I'll own the bench run and coordinate with your infra. Jordan will handle commercial.
[08:47] Jordan: Yep. We'll also include a proposed commercial for a 3-month reserved baseline with burst credits.
[08:54] Evan: Regarding encryption at rest: we must have customer-managed keys for some data.
[08:59] Camila: We support customer KMS for encryption at rest and in-transit TLS, plus HSM options for highest compliance.
[09:06] Sanjay: Any constraints on model weights residency? We need to ensure weights never leave our VPC for certain regs.
[09:13] Camila: For Private/on-prem we can support an air-gapped deployment or Private control plane so that models and logs live in your environment. For Dedicated hosted we keep weights in our managed infra but can offer VPC isolation and contractual guarantees.
[09:28] Maya: Ok makes sense.
[09:31] [10:00] Jordan: Quick recap then: we'll send pricing, SOC2 and network diagrams, and schedule the benchmark. Camila will run the trial. Any other questions?
[10:10] Sanjay: One more — what's the expected end-to-end latency for 13B long sequences (500 tokens)?
[10:17] Camila: That varies, but for 500 tokens full generation tail latency will be seconds; throughput oriented batching reduces cost but increases per-request latency — we'll show latency vs cost curves in the bench.
[10:28] Evan: Ok. That's reasonable.
[10:30] Jordan: Great. Let's capture action items.
[10:34] Camila: Action items: Jordan send pricing + contract template; Camila set up trial and benchmark; Sanjay share traces and prompt set.
[10:44] Maya: We'll route legal questions to Evan and our procurement lead.
[10:48] [39:00] (longer discussion about pricing scenarios, back-and-forth numbers — some transcription noise: "twenty five hundred vs twenty five hundred?" spelled odd)
[39:30] Camila: For billing, reserved GPU amortization example: X GPUs at $Y per month vs hosted egress, we'll attach a spreadsheet.
[40:05] Sanjay: Can you include a scenario where we keep baseline small (30%) and use burst heavily?
[40:11] Jordan: Yes we'll model three scenarios.
[40:15] Evan: Last question — who do we contact for security questionnaire?
[40:20] Jordan: I'll include our security lead's contact and we'll share the mismatch answers.
[40:25] Sanjay: Great. Thanks everyone.
[40:28] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up by Friday with docs and pricing and schedule the bench.
[40:33] Maya: Appreciate it.
[40:35] Camila: Thanks all.
[40:37] [51:30] Meeting end.

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hear: "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash"; product name "Dedicated" sometimes lowercase or mis-spelled as "dedictaed". References: shared deck (link: https://redwood.app/deck/dedicated-overview), benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.app/bench/novatech) — links provided for reference.
